_**Fallout 3**_ is a 2008 [action role-playing game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action_role-playing_game "Action role-playing game") developed by [Bethesda Game Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bethesda_Game_Studios "Bethesda Game Studios") and published by [Bethesda Softworks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bethesda_Softworks "Bethesda Softworks"). The game, which was released for [Microsoft Windows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Windows "Microsoft Windows"), [PlayStation 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_3 "PlayStation 3"), and [Xbox 360](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360 "Xbox 360"), is set in the [Washington metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_metropolitan_area "Washington metropolitan area") 200 years after a devastating [nuclear war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_war "Nuclear war"). The player controls a 19 year old character who leaves a [fallout shelter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_shelter "Fallout shelter") in search of their missing father. _Fallout 3_ features a freely explorable [open world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_world "Open world"), and the player can engage in combat with a variety of weapons. The player can also initiate conversations with [non-player characters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-player_character "Non-player character"), and depending on their actions, can affect how other characters perceive them.

The third major installment in the [_Fallout_ series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_/(franchise/) "Fallout (franchise)"), it is the first game to be developed by Bethesda after acquiring the rights to the franchise from [Interplay Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interplay_Entertainment "Interplay Entertainment"). Lead designer and writer [Emil Pagliarulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emil_Pagliarulo "Emil Pagliarulo") favored an oppressive and bleak atmosphere, and took inspiration from the dialogue in the [first _Fallout_ game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_/(video_game/) "Fallout (video game)"). Executive producer [Todd Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Todd_Howard "Todd Howard") wanted the combat to be a mix of real-time and turn-based combat, so that it would appeal to both [first-person shooter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First-person_shooter "First-person shooter") fans and role-playing game fans. Bethesda chose the Washington metropolitan area as the setting, as the studio was based in [Rockville, Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockville,_Maryland "Rockville, Maryland"), a city close to [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.")

_Fallout 3_ received a number of [Game of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Game_of_the_Year_awards "List of Game of the Year awards") awards, and is considered one of the [best video games ever made](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_video_games_ever_made "Best video games ever made"). Critics praised _Fallout 3_'s [open-ended gameplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-ended_gameplay "Open-ended gameplay") and flexible [character-leveling system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Level_up_/(video_gaming/) "Level up (video gaming)"), and the game shipped almost five million copies in its first week. It received post-launch support, with Bethesda releasing [five downloadable add-ons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3_downloadable_content "Fallout 3 downloadable content"). The game was met with controversy upon release in Australia, for the [recreational drug use](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recreational_drug_use "Recreational drug use") and the ability to be addicted to alcohol and other drugs; in India, for cultural and religious sentiments over the mutated cattle in the game being called [Brahmin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brahmin "Brahmin"), a [varna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varna_/(Hinduism/) "Varna (Hinduism)") (class) in [Hinduism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hinduism "Hinduism"); and in Japan, where a questline involving the potential detonation of a nuclear bomb in a prominent town was heavily altered. The game was followed by a spin-off, _[Fallout: New Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout:_New_Vegas "Fallout: New Vegas"),_ developed by [Obsidian Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obsidian_Entertainment "Obsidian Entertainment") in 2010. The fourth major installment in the _Fallout_ series, _[Fallout 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_4 "Fallout 4")_, was released in 2015.

_Fallout 3_ is an [action role-playing game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action_role-playing_game "Action role-playing game") that can be played from either a [first-person](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First-person_/(video_games/) "First-person (video games)") or [third-person](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third-person_/(video_games/) "Third-person (video games)") perspective.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-EGM_Review-1) It is set in the [Washington metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_metropolitan_area "Washington metropolitan area"), years after a [nuclear war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_war "Nuclear war") left much of the United States decimated.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-GamesRadar_Review-2) The player controls a 19 year old character who grew up in a [fallout shelter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_shelter "Fallout shelter") called [Vault 101](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vault_101 "Vault 101").[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-GamesRadar_Review-2) The goal of the game is to complete a series of [quests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quest_/(video_games/) "Quest (video games)") to find the character's father, who unexpectedly left Vault 101.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Guide_Book-3): 57  In addition to the main quests, the player can participate in optional unrelated quests known as side quests.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-GamesRadar_Review-2) _[GamesRadar+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GamesRadar%2B "GamesRadar+")_ critic Andy Kelly estimates there are over 100 hours of content in _Fallout 3_.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-GamesRadar_Review-2)

At the beginning of the game, the player can customize their character's physical appearance by choosing their gender and race.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-GameSpy_Preview-4)[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Ars_Technica-5) They can then allocate points into seven primary [attributes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attribute_/(role-playing_games/) "Attribute (role-playing games)"): strength, perception, endurance, charisma, intelligence, agility, and luck.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Ars_Technica-5) These attributes are known as S.P.E.C.I.A.L. stats, and range from 1 to 10.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Guide_Book-3): 4  Additionally, there are 13 secondary attributes whose point totals are affected by S.P.E.C.I.A.L. stats: barter, big guns, energy weapons, explosives, lockpick, medicine, melee weapons, repair, science, small guns, sneak, speech, and unarmed.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Guide_Book-3): 10  If the player has a high charisma stat for example, then they will be more proficient with the barter and speech skills at the beginning of the game.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Guide_Book-3): 6  The player can add more points into skill stats whenever they earn enough [experience points](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Experience_point "Experience point") to [level up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Experience_point#Level-based_progression "Experience point").[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Ars_Technica-5) Experience points can be earned through several methods, such as killing an enemy or completing a quest.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-GameSpy_Review-6) When the player reaches a new level, they can select a perk, which is a permanent beneficial upgrade.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Ars_Technica-5) For example, the perk Master Trader reduces the price of items sold by vendors by 25 percent.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Guide_Book-3): 18

[![Image 2](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/f/f2/Fallout_3_V.A.T.S._Screen.PNG/250px-Fallout_3_V.A.T.S._Screen.PNG)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Fallout_3_V.A.T.S._Screen.PNG)

While in combat, the player can use V.A.T.S. to pause the game and target specific body parts of an enemy.

_Fallout 3_ features an [open world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_world "Open world") map that the player can freely explore.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-IGN_Review-7) Locations the player can discover range from small settlements and abandoned buildings, to larger locations like the [Jefferson Memorial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jefferson_Memorial "Jefferson Memorial") and the [Washington Monument](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Monument "Washington Monument").[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-OXM_Interview-8) The player is equipped with a [wearable computer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wearable_computer "Wearable computer") called the [Pip-Boy 3000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pip-Boy "Pip-Boy").[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Ars_Technica-5) The device serves as a [menu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Menu_/(computing/) "Menu (computing)"), and allows the player to access items they have acquired; view detailed character statistics and active quests; and look at the map, which can be used to [fast travel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_travel "Fast travel") to previously discovered locations.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-GameSpy_Preview-4)[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Ars_Technica-5)[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Guide_Book-3): 32  The player can also utilize the Pip-Boy as a radio, letting them to listen to songs from the 1940s and 1950s on makeshift radio broadcasts.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Ars_Technica-5) While exploring, the player can recruit certain [non-playable characters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-playable_characters "Non-playable characters") as companions, who will accompany the player and assist them in combat.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Guide_Book-3): 38  There are a variety of weapons in the game, including standard guns, [energy-based guns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directed-energy_weapon "Directed-energy weapon"), melee weapons, and explosives.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Guide_Book-3): 33–34  While in combat, the player can utilize a gameplay mechanic known as V.A.T.S., which pauses the game and allows the player to target specific body parts of an enemy.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Eurogamer_Review-9) V.A.T.S. is dictated by a [statistic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statistic_/(role-playing_games/) "Statistic (role-playing games)") known as Action Points.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Eurogamer_Review-9) Each attack while in V.A.T.S. costs Action Points, and when the player runs out of Action Points they must wait a short period of time before they can use it again.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-GamesRadar_Review-2)

An important mechanic in _Fallout 3_ is the player's [karma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karma "Karma").[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-GameSpot_Review-10) Whenever the player commits an action that is deemed either good or bad, their karma will change accordingly.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-GameSpot_Review-10) For example, if the player provides water to a beggar, their karma increases.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-GameSpot_Review-10) Likewise, if the player breaks into a home, their karma decreases.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-GameSpot_Review-10) The player's karma affects how other characters perceive them.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Guide_Book-3): 30  Certain companions can only be recruited if the player meets the companion's karmic expectation.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Guide_Book-3): 30  Some non-recruitable characters will be more accepting of the player depending on their karma level,[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Guide_Book-3): 30  such as slavers, who will be more accepting to players with negative karma, and provide services that would not be available to players with neutral or positive karma.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Guide_Book-3): 30

[![Image 3](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/13/Jefferson_Memorial_At_Dusk_1.jpg/250px-Jefferson_Memorial_At_Dusk_1.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jefferson_Memorial_At_Dusk_1.jpg)

The plot of _Fallout 3_ revolves around a water purifier at the Jefferson Memorial.

_Fallout 3_ takes place in the year 2277, 200 years after a nuclear war between the United States and China. Some survivors of the war took refuge in high-tech [fallout shelters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_shelter "Fallout shelter") known as Vaults. The player character, nicknamed the Lone Wanderer, grew up in [Vault 101](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vault_101 "Vault 101"), located near [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.") After the Lone Wanderer's 19th birthday, their father, a scientist named James ([Liam Neeson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liam_Neeson "Liam Neeson")), leaves the Vault without explanation. The young vault dweller decides to track down their father and journeys the region in and around Washington, D.C., now known as the Capital Wasteland. Along the way, the Lone Wanderer learns about their father's background from other characters, including [Megaton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megaton_/(Fallout_3/) "Megaton (Fallout 3)") resident Colin Moriarty (Mike Rosson), [Galaxy News Radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galaxy_News_Radio "Galaxy News Radio") DJ Three Dog ([Erik Dellums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erik_Dellums "Erik Dellums")), and Rivet City scientist Madison Li (Jennifer Massey). Before the Lone Wanderer's birth, James and his wife Catherine had been working on Project Purity, in which a [water purifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water_purifier "Water purifier") built in the Jefferson Memorial would have purified the irradiated water in the [Tidal Basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tidal_Basin "Tidal Basin") and [Potomac River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potomac_River "Potomac River"). However, Catherine died during childbirth, and James abandoned the project to raise his child in Vault 101.

The Lone Wanderer finds and rescues James from a [virtual reality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtual_reality "Virtual reality") program run by overseer Stanislaus Braun ([Dee Bradley Baker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dee_Bradley_Baker "Dee Bradley Baker")) in [Vault 112](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vault_112 "Vault 112"). James reveals that he wanted to revive Project Purity and left Vault 101 to seek the Garden of Eden Creation Kit (G.E.C.K.), a powerful piece of technology intended to assist in rebuilding civilization after a nuclear war. When work on Project Purity resumes, the remnants of the United States government, known as the Enclave, intervene under the command of Colonel Augustus Autumn (Peter Gil). Its leader, President John Henry Eden ([Malcolm McDowell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malcolm_McDowell "Malcolm McDowell")), wants to inject the purifier with a deadly virus that will kill any mutated organisms who drink the water, including humans. James sacrifices himself to protect the purifier. In response, the Lone Wanderer enlists the help of the [Brotherhood of Steel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotherhood_of_Steel "Brotherhood of Steel"), a military organization that protects the residents of the Capital Wasteland. The Lone Wanderer finds the G.E.C.K. in Vault 87 but is captured by the Enclave and held in [Raven Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raven_Rock_Mountain_Complex "Raven Rock Mountain Complex"). They escape imprisonment and meet President Eden, who is revealed to be an [artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence "Artificial intelligence") program. Eden gives them a vial containing the virus and asks them to insert it into Project Purity. Afterwards, the Lone Wanderer leaves and optionally causes Eden to self destruct.

Together with the Brotherhood of Steel, the Lone Wanderer retakes the Jefferson Memorial from Autumn and learns the water purifier needs to be manually activated, or else it will shortly explode. Before James died, he flooded the control room with lethal amounts of radiation. The player can either sacrifice themselves to activate the purifier, optionally inserting the virus during the process; instruct Sarah Lyons, a Brotherhood member, to activate it instead; or do nothing and let it explode.

### Early development and writing

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fallout_3&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Early development and writing")\]

[![Image 4](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/22/Bethesda_Game_Studios_logo.svg/250px-Bethesda_Game_Studios_logo.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bethesda_Game_Studios_logo.svg)

The logo for Bethesda Game Studios

The origins of _Fallout 3_ date back to the cancellation of _[Van Buren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Van_Buren_/(video_game/) "Van Buren (video game)")_, which was intended to be the third game in the mainline [_Fallout_ series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_/(franchise/) "Fallout (franchise)").[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-TechRadar_Interview-11)[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-VG247_New_Vegas-12) Under the development of [Black Isle Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Isle_Studios "Black Isle Studios"), _Van Buren_ was to be set in [Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona "Arizona"), [Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado "Colorado"), [Nevada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nevada "Nevada"), and [Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah "Utah"), and would have included a mixture of [real-time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real-time_tactics "Real-time tactics") and [turn-based](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turn-based_tactics "Turn-based tactics") combat.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-VG247_New_Vegas-12)[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Retro_Gamer-13) Black Isle Studios' publisher [Interplay Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interplay_Entertainment "Interplay Entertainment") was struggling financially, and in December 2003 _Van Buren_ was cancelled.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-VG247_Black_Isle-14) In 2004, [Bethesda Softworks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bethesda_Softworks "Bethesda Softworks") purchased the rights to develop their own rendition of _Fallout 3_ from Interplay for $1,175,000 minimum guaranteed [advance against royalties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advance_against_royalties "Advance against royalties").[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-15) At the time, Bethesda was known for their work with _[The Elder Scrolls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Elder_Scrolls "The Elder Scrolls")_ series, but wanted to expand their catalogue with another project.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Retro_Gamer-13) According to developer Joel Burgess, Bethesda's holding company [ZeniMax Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ZeniMax_Media "ZeniMax Media") turned down multiple offers from other companies who wanted to work on the game.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-TechRadar_Interview-11) Burgess remarked, "The sense was we had to make our own game."[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-TechRadar_Interview-11)

Development on _Fallout 3_ began in late 2004 with a small team of around 10 people, as most of Bethesda's staff was busy working on _[The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Elder_Scrolls_IV:_Oblivion "The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion")_.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-GameSpot_X360-16) After the release of _The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion_ in 2006, the size of the team drastically increased.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-GameSpot_X360-16) Programmer Jean Simonet estimates that when development concluded, there were around 75 team members.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-TechRadar_Interview-11) Lead designer and writer [Emil Pagliarulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emil_Pagliarulo "Emil Pagliarulo") wrote the majority of the main story early in development, and when the team expanded, he allowed other designers to make rewrites and suggestions.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-TechRadar_Interview-11)[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Game_Developer_Interivew-17) This process exemplified Bethesda's decision to foster a more collaborative approach and allow developers to voice their opinions on various aspects of the game.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-TechRadar_Interview-11)[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Making_Of-18) Pagliarulo notes this approach differed from the rigid and "unhealthy" development of _The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion_, in which the developers had to follow the outline of the original design document regardless of their opinions.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Making_Of-18)

In multiple interviews, Bethesda developers noted the difficulty of working on a game from an established series they had no prior connection to.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-TechRadar_Interview-11)[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Game_Developer_Interivew-17)[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Making_Of-18) Product manager Pete Hines said Bethesda's mindset was to treat _Fallout 3_ as if they had worked on the original _Fallout_ games.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Making_Of-18) To this extent, they kept _Fallout 3_ an in-house production, and did not hire anyone who worked on the original games.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Eurogamer_Interview-19) Bethesda used the first _[Fallout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_/(video_game/) "Fallout (video game)")_ game as a model while designing _Fallout 3_.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Game_Developer_Interivew-17) Pagliarulo favored the oppressive and bleak atmosphere of the first _Fallout_ game in contrast to the excessive and [camp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_/(style/) "Camp (style)") dialogue of _[Fallout 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_2 "Fallout 2")_.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Game_Developer_Interivew-17)[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Making_Of-18) Pagliarulo wanted to instill a "rawness" to the dialogue, and included occasional profanity.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Game_Developer_Interivew-17) Another goal was to instill a sense of moral ambiguity whenever the player made an important decision.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Eurogamer_Interview-19) According to lead producer Gavin Carter, the karma mechanic was designed to let the player know the immediate consequences of their actions, and make the player question whether they made the right choice.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Eurogamer_Interview-19) The player character's father, James, was created as a moral compass, and would react to the player's previous actions.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Eurogamer_Interview-19)

### Gameplay and design

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fallout_3&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Gameplay and design")\]

A common joke among fans and journalists before the release of _Fallout 3_ was to describe it as "_Oblivion_ but with guns".[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-OXM_Interview-8)[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Shacknews_Interview-20) Due to Bethesda's previous oeuvre with [high fantasy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_fantasy "High fantasy") role-playing games, some players questioned whether _Fallout 3_ would simply be an iteration of _The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion_.[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Shacknews_Interview-20) Bethesda sought to incorporate elements of [first-person shooter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First-person_shooter "First-person shooter") games, while also allowing players to approach combat with a more tactical nuance commonly found in role-playing games.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Making_Of-18) Executive producer Todd Howard wanted the combat to be a mix of real-time and turn-based combat, which led to the creation of the V.A.T.S. system.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-TechRadar_Interview-11) Howard emphasized "cinematic" combat, and Simonet accomplished this goal by adding slow-motion effects whenever the player used V.A.T.S.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-TechRadar_Interview-11) The inspiration for the slow motion effects while in V.A.T.S. came from the slow motion replays of car crashes from the _[Burnout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnout_/(series/) "Burnout (series)")_ series.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Making_Of-18) Bethesda developers later discussed how they felt the shooting mechanics in _Fallout 3_ were one of the weaker elements of the game.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-TechRadar_Interview-11)[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-21) Burgess remarked, "We didn't really have first-person shooter experts, we didn’t really know ... If nothing else, it speaks to some of the ways we were successful that the mediocrity of the shooting didn't matter."[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-TechRadar_Interview-11)

The original setting for _Fallout 3_ was the [West Coast of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Coast_of_the_United_States "West Coast of the United States"), but early in development, the setting changed to the Washington metropolitan area.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Eurogamer_Interview-19) Pagliarulo said this decision stemmed from the adage "write what you know", as Bethesda was based in [Rockville, Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockville,_Maryland "Rockville, Maryland"), a city close to Washington, D.C.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Making_Of-18)[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Eurogamer_Interview-19) Burgess wanted Washington, D.C. to be a difficult location to explore, with harder enemies and more radiation.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-TechRadar_Interview-11) Due to how the [game engine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_engine "Game engine") worked, Washington, D.C. needed to be split into separate zones connected by the [Washington Metro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Metro "Washington Metro").[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-TechRadar_Interview-11) [Playtesters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Playtest "Playtest") routinely struggled to navigate the Metro, and complained the increased difficulty made the area less enjoyable.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-TechRadar_Interview-11) Bethesda attempted to remove the dividers separating the zones, but Burgess said the initial test did not show promise, and the idea was dropped.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-TechRadar_Interview-11) Burgess claims a proper test could have yielded a different result, and describes the entire Washington, D.C. area as "the big mistake I feel I made on \[_Fallout 3_\]".[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-TechRadar_Interview-11)

The original size of the _Fallout 3_ map was comparable to the size of the map in _The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion_.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-TechRadar_Interview-11) Bethesda incorporated various monuments from the Washington metropolitan area that would serve as visual landmarks to help the player navigate.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Making_Of-18) For example, when the player leaves Vault 101 at the beginning of the game, they see the Washington Monument in the distance, which was meant to help the player determine where Washington, D.C. was in relation to Vault 101.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Making_Of-18) About six months before release, Bethesda felt the map was too small.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-TechRadar_Interview-11) Whereas _The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion_ was able to hide the distance between locations with mountains and trees, _Fallout 3_'s barren wasteland setting meant that players were noticing locations too quickly.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-TechRadar_Interview-11) As a result, Bethesda increased the map size by roughly 20 percent, and spread out locations.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-TechRadar_Interview-11) Another map related issue brought up late in development was the fact that no one had modeled the [White House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House "White House").[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-GamesRadar_Video-22) As there was not enough time to create another significant location on the map, the decision was made to instead display the remnants of the White House amidst a giant crater, and explain that it was one of the locations targeted by nuclear attacks.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-GamesRadar_Video-22) Bethesda spread out enemy encounters so as to not inundate the player with excessive combat.[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Shacknews_Interview-20) In an attempt to keep the map unpredictable, they added random encounters the player can witness, such as a group of [contract killers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contract_killers "Contract killers") attacking a character, or a giant scorpion attacking a robot.[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Shacknews_Interview-20)

[Inon Zur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inon_Zur "Inon Zur") composed the score for _Fallout 3_, which was intended to balance traditional American music like [blues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blues "Blues") and [folk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_folk_music "American folk music"), with the powerful cadence of [military music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_music "Military music").[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-IGN_Zur-23) The goal was to showcase American life before the nuclear war while simultaneously emphasizing the theme of militant progress.[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-IGN_Zur-23) Zur was influenced by post-apocalyptic films like _[Mad Max 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mad_Max_2 "Mad Max 2")_ as well as [Vietnam War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam_War "Vietnam War") films like _[Full Metal Jacket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Full_Metal_Jacket "Full Metal Jacket")_.[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-IGN_Zur-23) The music is fully electronic, with occasional [samples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sampling_/(music/) "Sampling (music)") of live instruments.[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-IGN_Zur-23) When asked about the music, Zur said, "I wanted to create something that almost \[sounds as if it\] comes out of a boom box, rather than something that feels symphonic and heroic. Because all of the technology is sort of low-tech in _Fallout_, then the actual sound is representing and helping to represent this aspect, too."[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-IGN_Zur-23) In addition to the original soundtrack, _Fallout 3_ features licensed music that the player can listen to via in-game radio stations.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Kotaku_Music-24) The licensed music includes songs from artists such as [Roy Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Brown_/(blues_musician/) "Roy Brown (blues musician)"), [Billie Holiday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billie_Holiday "Billie Holiday"), [Billy Munn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Munn "Billy Munn"), [Cole Porter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cole_Porter "Cole Porter"), and [Bob Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Crosby "Bob Crosby").[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Kotaku_Music-24)

Over 40,000 lines of dialogue were recorded for _Fallout 3_, which at the time, set a [Guinness World Record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guinness_World_Record "Guinness World Record") for the most lines of dialogue in a single-player role-playing game.[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-25) Some celebrity actors were brought on to provide voice work, including [Liam Neeson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liam_Neeson "Liam Neeson") and [Malcolm McDowell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malcolm_McDowell "Malcolm McDowell").[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Making_Of-18) [Ron Perlman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Perlman "Ron Perlman") reprises his role as the narrator. In an interview with _[Edge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edge_/(magazine/) "Edge (magazine)")_, [Blindlight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindlight "Blindlight") manager Lev Chapelsky noted that former [president of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States") [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton") was jokingly offered a voice role, but the offer was swiftly rejected.[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-26) Hines later noted that even if Clinton had agreed, Bethesda would have not allowed him to provide voice work.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Kotaku_Clinton-27) Hines said, "In no way, shape or form, did we say is President Clinton is who we want for this role or \[tell Blindlight to\] go chase him."[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Kotaku_Clinton-27)

[![Image 5](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3f/Fallout_3_booth_on_Games_Convention_2008.jpg/250px-Fallout_3_booth_on_Games_Convention_2008.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Fallout_3_booth_on_Games_Convention_2008.jpg)

Bethesda's _Fallout 3_ booth at the 2008 [Games Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Games_Convention "Games Convention")

_Fallout 3_ was announced in July 2004, when Bethesda purchased the rights to the game from Interplay.[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-28) For years, there was little new information about the game, although Tor Thorsen of _[GameSpot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GameSpot "GameSpot")_ notes that interest in _Fallout 3_ rose significantly after the critical success of _The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion_.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-GameSpot_X360-16)[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-IGN_History-29) In April 2007, Bethesda published a teaser site for _Fallout 3_, and in June released the first trailer.[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-30)[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-GameSpy_Trailer-31) The trailer zooms out from inside a bus to show the ruins of Washington, D.C., accompanied by the song "[I Don't Want to Set the World on Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Don%27t_Want_to_Set_the_World_on_Fire "I Don't Want to Set the World on Fire")" by [the Ink Spots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ink_Spots "The Ink Spots").[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-GameSpy_Trailer-31) To promote the game, Bethesda partnered with [American Cinematheque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Cinematheque "American Cinematheque") and _[Geek Monthly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geek_Monthly "Geek Monthly")_ to hold a [film festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_festival "Film festival") titled _A Post-Apocalyptic Film Festival Presented by Fallout 3_.[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Kotaku_Films-32) The festival showcased six post-apocalyptic films: _[12 Monkeys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/12_Monkeys "12 Monkeys")_, _[A Boy and His Dog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Boy_and_His_Dog_/(1975_film/) "A Boy and His Dog (1975 film)")_, _[Damnation Alley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Damnation_Alley_/(film/) "Damnation Alley (film)")_, _[The Last Man on Earth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Last_Man_on_Earth_/(1964_film/) "The Last Man on Earth (1964 film)")_, _[The Omega Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Omega_Man "The Omega Man")_, and _[Wizards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wizards_/(film/) "Wizards (film)")_.[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Kotaku_Films-32) The game had a marketing budget of $13 million.[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-33)

_Fallout 3_ was released for [Microsoft Windows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Windows "Microsoft Windows"), [PlayStation 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_3 "PlayStation 3"), and [Xbox 360](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_360 "Xbox 360") on October 28, 2008 in North America, October 30 in Europe and Australia, and December 4 in Japan.[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-34)[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-GameSpot_Sales-35) In its first week of release, _Fallout 3_ had sold 4.7 million copies worldwide, and grossed $300 million.[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-GameSpot_Sales-35) _Fallout 3_ outsold every previous _Fallout_ game combined, and sales were 57% stronger than _The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion_ in its first week of release.[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-36) The market research firm Electronic Entertainment Design and Research estimated that by 2015, the game had sold 12.4 million copies worldwide.[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-37)

Due to its content, some versions of _Fallout 3_ were subject to censorship.[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Ars_Technica_Censor-38) The initial Australian version was refused classification by the [Australian Classification Board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Classification_Board "Australian Classification Board") (ACB) due to its realistic depiction of drug use.[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-39) As it is illegal to distribute or purchase an Australian game without an ACB classification, Bethesda replaced all instances of the drug [morphine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morphine "Morphine") with a generic drug, and removed the drug injection animation.[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Shacknews_Censor-40)[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-41) Bethesda further altered every version of _Fallout 3_ to accommodate for these changes.[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Shacknews_Censor-40) Another version of the game subject to censorship was the Japanese version, due to its depiction of nuclear weaponry.[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Ars_Technica_Censor-38) A quest that allowed the player to either defuse or detonate a nuclear warhead was altered so that it was impossible to detonate it, and the name of a weapon was changed.[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Ars_Technica_Censor-38) Excess blood and gore were removed from the German version by the [Federal Department for Media Harmful to Young Persons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Department_for_Media_Harmful_to_Young_Persons "Federal Department for Media Harmful to Young Persons"),[\[42\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-42) and Microsoft chose not to release _Fallout 3_ in India due to perceived "cultural sensitivities".[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Kotaku_India-43)[\[A\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-44)

In 2023, a leaked [financial forecast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_forecast "Financial forecast") presentation indicated that Bethesda was working on a [remaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game_remake "Video game remake") of _Fallout 3_.[\[44\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-PC_Gamer_Remaster-45) The presentation stated that the remaster was scheduled for a 2024 release, although _[PC Gamer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PC_Gamer "PC Gamer")_ notes that the release projection predated the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), which has likely delayed development.[\[44\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-PC_Gamer_Remaster-45)

### Downloadable content

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fallout_3&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Downloadable content")\]

_Fallout 3_ was supported with five [downloadable content](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downloadable_content "Downloadable content") (DLC) add-ons.[\[45\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Kotaku_DLC-46) The first DLC was _Operation: Anchorage_, which takes place inside a virtual reality simulation that depicts a battle between United States and Chinese soldiers in [Anchorage, Alaska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anchorage,_Alaska "Anchorage, Alaska").[\[46\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-47) The second DLC was _The Pitt_.[\[47\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Eurogamer_Pitt-48) Set in [Pittsburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh "Pittsburgh"), the player infiltrates a slaver compound, and looks for a cure for the mutant disease affecting the slave population.[\[47\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Eurogamer_Pitt-48) The third DLC, _Broken Steel_, takes place immediately after the events of main story, and revolves around the Brother of Steel's campaign to eliminate the remaining Enclave soldiers.[\[48\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-49) The fourth DLC, _Point Lookout_, is set in [Point Lookout State Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Point_Lookout_State_Park "Point Lookout State Park"), where the player investigates the disappearance of a young girl.[\[49\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-IGN_Point_Lookout-50) In the final DLC, _Mothership Zeta_, the player is [abducted by aliens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abducted_by_aliens "Abducted by aliens"), and must escape from a [UFO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFO "UFO").[\[49\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-IGN_Point_Lookout-50)

Development on the DLC add-ons began roughly two months before _Fallout 3_'s release.[\[45\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Kotaku_DLC-46) Only three add-ons were initially planned, but due to player feedback the number was increased to five.[\[45\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Kotaku_DLC-46) Initially, the DLC add-ons were not released for the PlayStation 3 version.[\[50\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Edge_Exclusivity-51) [Lazard Capital Markets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lazard_Capital_Markets "Lazard Capital Markets") analyst Colin Sebastian speculated that this was likely the result of a deal with Bethesda by [Sony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony "Sony")'s competitor, [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft").[\[50\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Edge_Exclusivity-51) Howard offered a different explanation, and said it was due to more Xbox 360 owners paying for _The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion_ DLC than PlayStation 3 owners.[\[49\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-IGN_Point_Lookout-50) By 2009, all five add-ons were made available to PlayStation 3 owners.[\[49\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-IGN_Point_Lookout-50)

_Fallout 3_ was well received by critics.[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-IGN_History-29) On the [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator") website [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), the Microsoft Windows version of _Fallout 3_ was assigned the game a weighted average critic score of 91/100, the PlayStation 3 version a 90/100, and the Xbox 360 version a 93/100.[\[51\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Metacritic_PC-52)[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Metacritic_PS3-53)[\[53\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Metacritic_X360-54) The Xbox 360 version is tied with _[Braid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Braid_/(video_game/) "Braid (video game)")_, _[Gears of War 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gears_of_War_2 "Gears of War 2")_, and _[Super Smash Bros. Brawl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Smash_Bros._Brawl "Super Smash Bros. Brawl")_ as the fourth highest rated game from 2008 on Metacritic.[\[58\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-60)

_[1UP.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1UP.com "1UP.com")_'s Demian Linn praised its open-ended gameplay and flexible character-leveling system. While the V.A.T.S. system was called fun, enemy encounters were said to suffer from a lack of precision in real-time combat and little variety in enemy types. The review concluded, _Fallout 3_ is a "hugely ambitious game that doesn't come around very often."[\[59\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-1UP.com_review-61) _[IGN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IGN "IGN")_ editor Erik Brudvig praised the game's "minimalist" sound design, observing how "you might find yourself with nothing but the sound of wind rustling through decaying trees and blowing dust across the barren plains ... _Fallout 3_ proves that less can be more." The review noted that the "unusual amount of realism" combined with the "endless conversation permutations" produces "one of the most truly interactive experiences of the generation."[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-IGN_Review-7) In a review of the game for _[Kotaku](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kotaku "Kotaku")_, Mike Fahey commented: "While [Inon Zur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inon_Zur "Inon Zur")'s score is filled with epic goodness, the real stars of _Fallout 3_'s music are the vintage songs from the 1940s."[\[60\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-kotaku-62)

[Tim Cain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Cain "Tim Cain"), _[Fallout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_/(video_game/) "Fallout (video game)")_ and _[Fallout 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_2 "Fallout 2")_ [game director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_director "Game director"), praised the art direction and the attention to details but did not like the way the endings were not enough constructed around player's actions and decisions.[\[61\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-63) He was also critical of how _Fallout 3_ recycled plot elements from the first two games, such as Super Mutants and the Enclave, saying that if his company, [Troika Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troika_Games "Troika Games"), had acquired the license, he would have come up with a completely original story for the East coast. [Chris Avellone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Avellone "Chris Avellone"), _[Fallout 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_2 "Fallout 2")_'s main writer, described the game as having "enough options and tools at \[his\] disposal to insure \[_[sic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sic "Sic")_\] \[he\] was having fun no matter what the challenges", praising the immersion in _Fallout_'s world, the success in carrying on the legacy of the previous two games, and the fulfilling open-world component; he criticized the writing of some characters and some of gameplay's choices in balancing the skills of the [player character](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Player_character "Player character").[\[62\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-64) Will Tuttle of _[GameSpy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GameSpy "GameSpy")_ commended the game for its "engaging storyline, impeccable presentation, and hundreds of hours of addictive gameplay."[\[63\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-65) Although _[Edge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edge_/(magazine/) "Edge (magazine)")_ awarded the game 7 out of 10, in a later anniversary issue it placed the game 37th in a "100 best games to play today" list, saying "_Fallout 3_ empowers, engages and rewards to extents that few games have ever achieved."[\[64\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Edge_list-66)

Some criticisms concerned the bugs in regards to the physics and crashes, some of which broke quests and prevented progression.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-IGN_Review-7) The AI and stiff character animations are another common point of criticism,[\[65\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Shacknews_review-67)[\[66\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-68)[\[67\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-PSM3_review-69) as is the ending.[\[65\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Shacknews_review-67)[\[68\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-70) _Edge_ stated that "the game is cumbersome in design and frequently incompetent in the details of execution", taking particular issue with the nakedness of the [HUD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HUD_/(video_gaming/) "HUD (video gaming)"), the clarity of the menu interface, and that the smaller problems are carried over from _[Oblivion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Elder_Scrolls_IV:_Oblivion "The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion")_. _Edge_ liked the central story but said "the writing isn't quite as consistent as the ideas that underpin" and that the "voice-acting is even less reliable."[\[54\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Edge_Review-55)

> It's not a _Fallout_ game. It's not even a game inspired by _Fallout_, as I had hoped. It's a game that contains a loose assortment of familiar _Fallout_ concepts and names ... Electricity, pre-war electronic equipment, powered and still working computers (just think about that for a second), working cola & snack machines, weapons, ammo, scrap metal (needed by many), and even unlooted first aid boxes are everywhere.

—Vince D. Weller, long-time _No Mutants Allowed_ member, former RPG news site director, and lead developer of _[The Age of Decadence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Age_of_Decadence "The Age of Decadence")_[\[69\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-destructoid_shutup-71)[\[70\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-72)

Not all fans were happy with the direction the _Fallout_ series was taken in after its acquisition by Bethesda.[\[71\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Fallout_Fans-73) Notorious for their support of the series' first two games, _[Fallout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_/(video_game/) "Fallout (video game)")_ and _[Fallout 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_2 "Fallout 2")_, members centered on one of the oldest _Fallout_ [fansites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fansite "Fansite"), _No Mutants Allowed_, have criticized departures from the original games' stories, gameplay mechanics and setting.[\[72\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-escapist_fringe-74)[\[73\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-kotaku_relent-75) Criticisms include the prevalence of unspoiled food after 200 years, the survival of wood-framed dwellings following a [nuclear blast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_blast "Nuclear blast"), and the ubiquity of Super Mutants at early levels in the game.[\[73\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-kotaku_relent-75) Also criticized are the quality of the game's writing, its relative lack of [verisimilitude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Verisimilitude "Verisimilitude"), the switch to a first-person action game format, and the level of reactiveness of the surrounding game world to player actions.[\[73\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-kotaku_relent-75)[\[74\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-76)[\[75\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-77) In response, [James Stephanie Sterling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Stephanie_Sterling "James Stephanie Sterling") of _[Destructoid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Destructoid "Destructoid")_ called fan groups like _No Mutants Allowed_ "selfish" and "arrogant", stating that a new audience deserves a chance to play a _Fallout_ game; and that if the series had stayed the way it was back in 1997, new titles would never have been made and brought to market.[\[69\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-destructoid_shutup-71) Luke Winkie of _[Kotaku](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kotaku "Kotaku")_ tempers these sentiments, saying that it is a matter of ownership; and that in the case of _Fallout 3_, hardcore fans of the original series witnessed their favorite games become transformed into something else.[\[73\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-kotaku_relent-75)

After its release, _Fallout 3_ won numerous awards from gaming journalists and websites.[\[76\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-78) It was awarded Game of the Year by _[Gamasutra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamasutra "Gamasutra")_, _[GamesRadar+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GamesRadar%2B "GamesRadar+")_, GameSpy, _IGN_, and _[UGO Networks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UGO_Networks "UGO Networks")_.[\[C\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-84) The game also won Xbox 360 Game of the Year from GameSpy, _IGN_, and _Official Xbox Magazine_, and PC Game of the Year from _[GamePro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GamePro "GamePro")_, GameSpy, _GameSpot_, and _[GameTrailers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GameTrailers "GameTrailers")_.[\[D\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-92) At the 2009 [Golden Joystick Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Joystick_Awards "Golden Joystick Awards"), _Fallout 3_ won Ultimate Game of the Year.[\[89\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-93) It also won Game of the Year along with Best Writing at the [Game Developers Choice Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_Developers_Choice_Awards "Game Developers Choice Awards").[\[90\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-94) During the [12th Annual Interactive Achievement Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/12th_Annual_Interactive_Achievement_Awards "12th Annual Interactive Achievement Awards"), the [Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Interactive_Arts_%26_Sciences "Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences") awarded _Fallout 3_ with [Role-Playing Game of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D.I.C.E._Award_for_Role-Playing_Game_of_the_Year "D.I.C.E. Award for Role-Playing Game of the Year") and [Outstanding Achievement in Original Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D.I.C.E._Award_for_Outstanding_Achievement_in_Story "D.I.C.E. Award for Outstanding Achievement in Story"), and nominated it for [Overall Game of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D.I.C.E._Award_for_Game_of_the_Year "D.I.C.E. Award for Game of the Year"), Computer Game of the Year, Console Game of the Year, [Outstanding Achievement in Game Direction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D.I.C.E._Award_for_Outstanding_Achievement_in_Game_Direction "D.I.C.E. Award for Outstanding Achievement in Game Direction"), [Outstanding Achievement in Game Design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D.I.C.E._Award_for_Outstanding_Achievement_in_Game_Design "D.I.C.E. Award for Outstanding Achievement in Game Design"), and [Outstanding Achievement in Gameplay Engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D.I.C.E._Award_for_Outstanding_Technical_Achievement "D.I.C.E. Award for Outstanding Technical Achievement").[\[91\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-95)

Some critics have referred to _Fallout 3_ as one of the best games in the _Fallout_ series,[\[E\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-100) and as one of the [greatest games of all time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greatest_games_of_all_time "Greatest games of all time").[\[F\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-105) It is also considered one of the defining games of the [seventh generation of video game consoles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seventh_generation_of_video_game_consoles "Seventh generation of video game consoles"), which generally encompasses the years 2005 to 2013.[\[100\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Eurogamer_Games_of_Decade-106)[\[101\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-IGN_Generation-107)[\[102\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-108) _Fallout 3_ was included in _[The Art of Video Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Art_of_Video_Games "The Art of Video Games")_ exhibit at [Smithsonian American Art Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smithsonian_American_Art_Museum "Smithsonian American Art Museum"), where it was described as the defining [adventure game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adventure_game "Adventure game") for current computers.[\[103\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-109) In an article about the seventh generation of video game consoles, _Eurogamer_'s Will Porter described _Fallout 3_ as "a perfect meld of the old and the new ... The way _Fallout 3_ strode out, blinked beneath an unfamiliar sun and went on to thrive, genuinely made it one of the greatest experiences of this generation."[\[100\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Eurogamer_Games_of_Decade-106) _IGN_ gave similar commentary, and stated, "It's a truly special western role-playing game, one with a deep, post-apocalyptic plot, memorable characters, and an emphasis on choice".[\[101\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-IGN_Generation-107)

_Fallout 3_'s open world map is often cited as the game's greatest achievement.[\[100\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Eurogamer_Games_of_Decade-106)[\[104\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Kotaku_RPG-110)[\[105\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-PC_Gamer_Map-111) Its portrayal of 1950s American culture contrasted by the devastation of nuclear war helped _Fallout 3_ stand apart from contemporary high fantasy role-playing games like _[The Elder Scrolls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Elder_Scrolls "The Elder Scrolls")_ and _[Gothic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothic_/(series/) "Gothic (series)")_.[\[100\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Eurogamer_Games_of_Decade-106)[\[106\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-112) Journalists have also noted how the map emphasized exploration, and allowed players to find unique side quests and scenes of environmental storytelling.[\[100\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Eurogamer_Games_of_Decade-106)[\[107\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-RPS_Map-113) Khee Hoon Chan of _[Rock Paper Shotgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_Paper_Shotgun "Rock Paper Shotgun")_ remarked, "The _Fallout 3_ world is probably better traversed when you abandon all pretense of trying to find your father, and wander about the endless wilderness as a roaming wayfarer, discovering these vignettes of humanity's perseverance after a global catastrophe."[\[107\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-RPS_Map-113) Jeremy Peel of _[PCGamesN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PCGamesN "PCGamesN")_ argues that _Fallout 3_'s depiction of Washington, D.C. revolutionized video game exploration due to its non-linear design. Peel wrote, "Part of _Fallout 3_'s legacy lies in setting the concept of a videogame dungeon free. Bethesda's D.C. allows you to approach its dangers from different directions, in different orders, and still find a satisfying loop you can recognize as dungeon-spelunking."[\[108\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-PCGamesN-114)

In the years since its release, the initial overwhelming praise bestowed on _Fallout 3_ has somewhat subsided.[\[109\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-TheGamer-115) Retrospective commentary surrounding _Fallout 3_ often focuses on the writing, which some players and journalists have bemoaned for the lack of choices the player can make to affect the story and unrealistic character decisions.[\[109\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-TheGamer-115)[\[110\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Kotaku_Retrospective-116)[\[111\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Hardcore_Gaming-117) For example, at the end of the game when the player can choose to sacrifice themself to activate the purifier, they are unable to ask a companion to do it instead, even if the companion is immune to radiation.[\[111\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Hardcore_Gaming-117)[\[112\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-118) _Fallout 3_'s successor, _[Fallout: New Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout:_New_Vegas "Fallout: New Vegas")_, introduced multiple questlines the player can follow to complete the game and replaced the karma system with reputation among specific factions.[\[113\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Push_Square-119) Due to its expanded role-playing mechanics, some players and journalists not only favor _Fallout: New Vegas_, but also deride _Fallout 3_ in comparison.[\[109\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-TheGamer-115) In response to the backlash, journalist Jade King wrote, "It feels elitist to suddenly pigeonhole it as some sort of failure ... Back in 2008, _Fallout 3_ set a new benchmark for what open world \[role-playing games\] were capable of. We view it with such derision in hindsight, because Bethesda never really moved on from it.[\[109\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-TheGamer-115)

_Fallout 3_ brought the _Fallout_ series into the mainstream.[\[114\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Washington_Post-120)[\[113\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Push_Square-119) Billy Studholme of _[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Washington_Post "The Washington Post")_ wrote, "Before _Fallout 3_, there was no _Fallout_ as we know it today. The game blew the hinges off the franchise in the best way."[\[114\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Washington_Post-120) Due to the tepid reception toward the spin-off games _[Fallout Tactics: Brotherhood of Steel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_Tactics:_Brotherhood_of_Steel "Fallout Tactics: Brotherhood of Steel")_ and _[Fallout: Brotherhood of Steel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout:_Brotherhood_of_Steel "Fallout: Brotherhood of Steel")_, and the cancellation of the _Van Buren_ project, the series stagnated in the mid 2000s.[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-IGN_History-29) Bethesda's decision to swap the [isometric graphics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isometric_graphics "Isometric graphics") of the older games with 3D graphics as well as release the game on consoles helped _Fallout 3_ reach a wider audience.[\[114\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Washington_Post-120)[\[115\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-Eurogamer_History-121) Maxwell McGee of _GamesRadar+_ also notes that Bethesda made _Fallout 3_ more accessible to new players.[\[116\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-GamesRadar_New_Players-122) McGee stated, "It's a guided experience that expertly introduces the _Fallout_ universe without leaving you lost in the wasteland."[\[116\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_3#cite_note-GamesRadar_New_Players-122)

15.content:
### Steps  

1.  Find Dad.
2.  Find and speak to Betty.
3.  Make Timmy Neusbaum cry.
4.  Report back to Betty.
5.  Break up the Rockwells' marriage, without killing either of them.
6.  Report back to Betty.
7.  Arrange a creative death for Mabel Henderson.
8.  Report back to Betty.
9.  Retrieve the mask and knife from behind the Abandoned House.
10.  Kill all the residents of Tranquility Lane.
11.  Report back to Betty.
12.  Exit Tranquility Lane.
13.  Talk to Dad.

### Items

None.

Part 1
------

Just what the hell is going on here!? Why, you're in virtual reality, of course! Welcome to Tranquility Lane, a rather ingenious creation for nuclear survivors to live happily in lives they once knew. But you're not here to enjoy yourself, and you're not here to make friends. You're here to get to the bottom of what's going on, and to find your father. Feel free to take a few minutes to explore, talking to whomever you want and entering whatever house you'd like. Most everyone has nice things to say and are enjoying life. This is a real Leave It To Beaver moment, we know. **And PLEASE, don't e-mail us about the alternate route. As the box below indicates, there is a good karma way through. We cover the bad karma route here.**

### Notice

After putting up this section of the guide, we received _massive_ amounts of e-mail from you guys, the readers. Therefore, **please keep in mind that our detailed walkthrough for this section is considered the "evil" way of doing it**. To accomplish this part of the game without losing any karma, it's actually easy. Head to the "abandoned house" in the simulation. Here, you'll find five items in the house that must be activated in a certain order (listen for the chimes when the item is activated to see if you're doing it in the right order or not). Once activated properly, a computer will reveal itself. Activate the computer program when prompted to do so, and a communist invasion of the simulation will occur, killing everyone within _for_ you, allowing you to ultimately escape with unharmed karma.

Ultimately, however, you'll find that no one has any idea where your father is, and what's more, you seem trapped in this virtual reality. That's where a little girl named Betty comes into play, because you need to find Betty and speak with her. She can be found at the center of the circular neighborhood in a simple playground. Upon speaking with her, she'll show you how bossy she can be, and demand that you play a game with her. There's simply no way around it, you have to agree. And this is when she asks you to make her playmate, Timmy, cry. (If you refuse, you have to figure out a Betty-less way to get out of here, which is possible, but far less fun).

There are a few ways to make Timmy cry, but the easiest (and most sickly rewarding) way is to kill his mother. Timmy's family's house is the one with the lemonade stand in front of it. Head into the house, simply letting yourself in, and seek out Timmy's mom. Then, with your fists, do her in, chasing her around the house as she screams for mercy. This may be sick, but it's necessary (though you can find more subtle ways to make Timmy cry if you must). When you've done the deed, report back to Betty, who will allow you to ask her one question before the game continues. That's when you realize she isn't a little girl at all, but is instead being controlled by an unknown man named Dr. Stanislaus Braun.

Braun asks you next to break up the otherwise happy marriage of the Rockwells. But, you can't kill them, so you need to figure out another way to do it. The Rockwells' house is a house without a fence in front of it, with a slightly-overgrown yard, trees in the front, and a gnome on the small concrete stoop. Enter the house and speak with the Rockwells. You can pry some about their marriage, but they won't be too happy about it. But now that you've introduced yourself to them, it's time to break up their happy marriage. Sorry folks, it has to be done.

Again, there are a few ways this can be done, but this is what we did. Leave the Rockwells' residence and, while facing it, look to your left. The neighboring house there is the Simpson household. Enter the house, and head on upstairs into the master bedroom. Examine the queen-sized bed there, and you'll discover some underwear. Grab these undergarments and run back outside and head into the Rockwell's residence once more. Go into the basement of the house, approach the desk in the corner, and examine it to place the underwear on it. Where are we going with this?

Once the underwear is on the desk, head upstairs and tell Mrs. Rockwell that you saw something in the basement she needs to see. While she's curious what you were doing in the basement, you can insist that she come downstairs with you and check out what's down there. She agrees. Go back into the basement and Mrs. Rockwell will automatically be in pursuit. Approach the desk and go through the motions, telling her that Mr. Rockwell is either cheating, or insinuating that he could be a cross-dresser. Either way, Mrs. Rockwell is distressed, running upstairs, out of the house and gone seemingly forever. The distressed Mr. Rockwell will have no idea what hit him!

Part 2
------

Go back and see Betty in the same location she's been this entire time -- the playground at the center of the small neighborhood. She'll be most thankful of the work you've been doing, and you can continue to pry with the doctor controlling her about just what's going on, learning just a little more about the situation here. But Betty -- we mean, Dr. Stanislaus Braun -- has another activity for you. This time, he wants you to kill Mabel Henderson. And you have to do it in a clever way, _not_ with your fists. Oh my!

Mabel Henderson's house is located on the other side of the Simpson house (the Rockwell house being on the _other_ side, thus the Simpson house being in the middle of the two). Head on in there and, before doing anything, go into the kitchen. Examine the stove and _fiddle_ with the pilot light. Just what's going on here? Well, this is a clever way to kill Mabel (though there are others, if you can figure them out). Speak with Mabel hereafter and ask her to make you one of her famous pies. She'll agree and head into the kitchen to pre-heat the oven. When she does this, she'll be met with an untimely death. Poor Mrs. Henderson, flaming to death on the kitchen floor.

Your time on the demented Tranquility Lane is coming to a close. After Mabel's demise, go back and speak with Betty once more, who will commend you on a job well-done. She tells you there's only one thing left to do, and then you can have whatever you want. She wants you to kill everyone -- _everyone_ -- on Tranquility Lane. Oh my! And doing so will require that you grab a mask and knife that Betty has hidden for you near a doghouse at the abandoned house on Tranquility Lane. So what are you waiting for? Go grab your gear!

Seek out the abandoned house -- there's a gate around the house, no one inside, and a doghouse to the right of the house. Examine the doghouse and you'll find yourself automatically equipped with a creepy mask and a gigantic butcher's knife which will be used to execute everyone on Tranquility Lane. Then, try to systematically go around and kill everyone in each house, following each character if they run away from you, _especially_ if they run outside (this will confuse things intensely if you let them go).

Having fun? Well, we hope so, because you're losing a hell of a lot of karma from doing this, but you need to get out of this virtual insanity (an odd Jamiroquai reference) and get back to your primary mission. So, killing everyone is your only choice. You don't have to waste time going back to Betty each time you kill someone to see if you killed everyone -- as long as you pay close attention to your screen, you can see that the objective has been successfully completed when the last person is killed (it's important to pay attention since you can't consult your Pip-Boy to see what's going on).

When the last person is killed, visit Betty at the playground and she'll congratulate you on a job well done. Since you've done everything the evil doctor has asked, he's agreed to let you _and_ your father (who was the dog in the playground) out of virtual reality, where they can thereafter return to the Capital Wasteland. Good to have all of that fake (yet real) blood off of your hands.

When you're back in reality, exit your virtual reality pod and engage your father in conversation. This can be a lengthy conversation, as you can poke and prod your father for all sorts of interesting information about Project Purity, your mother, Vault 101, and the realities of this post-nuclear world. Once you're done speaking with him, you can then follow him as he books it out of Vault 112 and back to the surface. Once on the surface, this mission comes to an end. It's time to head back to Rivet City and meet up with the famed Dr. Li once more.

### Up Next: The Waters of Life

### Was this guide helpful?

### In This Guide

Fallout 3: Why the Experiment in Vault 112 is So Easy to Hijack
===============================================================

![Image 8: Fallout 3 Stanislaus Braun Vault 112 tranquility lane statis pod](https://static0.gamerantimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/Fallout-3-Why-The-Experiment-in-Vault-112-is-so-Easy-to-Hijack.jpg?&fit=crop&w=1600&h=900)

[![Image 9: 4](https://static0.gamerantimages.com/wordpress%2Fwp-content%2Fauthors%2F634f59ce18665-DP.png?fit=crop&w=90&h=90)](https://gamerant.com/author/annakatrina-cerafica/)

By[Anna C](https://gamerant.com/author/annakatrina-cerafica/)

Published Mar 18, 2022

Freelance writer who enjoys overanalyzing games. If she's not gaming, she's probably tending to her drama queen of a dog. Other times, she's studying for her Master's Degree in Comparative Literature. 

[Sign in to your Game Rant account](https://gamerant.com/fallout-3-vault-112-vr-experiment-hijack-easy-reason-lore-explained/)

[Add Us On](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=gamerant.com "Add Us On")
